title: Consumer Expectations Survey Report: 1st Quarter 2026
venue: Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas Consumer Expectations Survey
tldr: Philippine consumer sentiment improved in Q1 2026 as households were less pessimistic about current conditions, though year-ahead outlook softened amid inflation and corruption concerns.
problem_and_motivation: Understanding Filipino household consumer expectations is essential for monetary policy and economic planning. The CES provides quarterly advance indication of consumer sentiments across income groups and geographic areas, capturing spending, savings, inflation, and debt outlooks that inform economic forecasting.
approach: Quarterly stratified multi-stage probability sample of 5,358 households nationwide drawn from the PSA 2023 Geo-Enabled Master Sample.
Confidence indices computed as percentage of affirmative responses minus percentage of negative responses across three component indices.
Household income groups defined as low (below P10,000), middle (P10,000 to P29,999), and high (above P30,000) monthly family income.
Geographic disaggregation between NCR (2,434 respondents) and Areas Outside the NCR (2,924 respondents).
Sentiment assessed for current quarter, next quarter, and next 12 months across economic condition, family financial situation, and family income.
Survey conducted 22 January to 5 February 2026, prior to the onset of the Middle East conflict.
Cross-country benchmarking against consumer confidence indices from 12 reference economies.
Diffusion Index methodology applied to inflation, peso borrowing rate, exchange rate, and unemployment rate expectations.
findings: num: Current-quarter confidence index improved from -22.2% in Q4 2025 to -15.8% in Q1 2026.
num: Year-ahead confidence index decreased from 11.8% to 9.6%, reflecting less upbeat consumer outlook.
num: 73.9% of saving households planned to set aside less than 10% of monthly family income.
num: Saving intention index increased from 4.6% to 12.4%, indicating more optimistic savings sentiment.
num: Year-ahead inflation forecast rose slightly from 2.6% to 2.7%, remaining below BSP 3.0% target.
num: 96.1% of OFW households used remittances for food and other household needs.
num: Response rate was 98.3% in NCR and 98.6% in AONCR, with sampling error margins of plus or minus 1.3% nationally.
num: Spending outlook index for next quarter declined from 43.7% to 40.3%, less upbeat across most consumer items.
num: Big-ticket buying sentiment improved from -66.2% to -64.0% for current quarter.
num: 6.6% of households planned to buy real property within the next 12 months, up from 6.2%.
key_figures_tables: Figure 1: Overall Consumer Confidence Index Philippines Q1 2021 to Q1 2026 -> Consumer sentiment less negative at -15.8%.
Figure 2: Consumer Confidence Index by Component Index -> All three components less pessimistic in Q1 2026.
Figure 3: Consumer Confidence Index by Income Group -> Confidence improved across all income groups.
Figure 4: Consumer Confidence Index for NCR and AONCR -> Both regions less pessimistic in Q1 2026.
Figure 5: Next Quarter Expenditure Outlook on Goods and Services -> Spending outlook less upbeat at 40.3%.
Figure 6: Sentiment on Buying Big-Ticket Items -> Buying sentiment less negative across categories.
Figure 7: Saving Intention Index -> More optimistic at 12.4% versus 4.6% in Q4 2025.
Figure 8: Usage of OFW Remittances -> 96.1% allocated to food and household needs.
Figure 10: Borrowing Intention Index -> Borrowing outlook improved, less negative for both periods.
Figure 11: Percentage of Respondents by Income Group -> High-income group largest at 40.3%.

key_equations.explanation: Confidence Index computed as affirmative minus negative response percentages.
Overall consumer outlook index is average of three component confidence indices.

definitions.definition: Consumer Expectations Survey, a quarterly BSP survey of approximately 5,500 Philippine households.
Confidence Index, the percentage of affirmative responses minus the percentage of negative responses for a given indicator.
Diffusion Index, used to measure the direction of expectations for economic indicators.
National Capital Region, the metropolitan area encompassing Metro Manila.
Areas Outside the National Capital Region, covering the rest of the Philippines.
Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas, the central bank of the Philippines.
Overseas Filipino Worker, a Philippine national working abroad.
Philippine Statistics Authority, the national statistical agency.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This report provides quarterly empirical data on Filipino household consumer expectations covering spending, savings, inflation, and borrowing outlooks across income groups and geographic regions. The CES methodology establishes a standardized framework for measuring consumer sentiment using confidence indices computed from household survey responses. The income-group disaggregation and longitudinal quarterly tracking enable analysis of financial behavioral patterns across demographic segments. Cross-country benchmarking with 12 reference economies places Philippine consumer sentiment in international context.
directly_justifies: Current-quarter confidence index improved from -22.2% to -15.8% in Q1 2026.
73.9% of saving households planned to set aside less than 10% of monthly family income.
Year-ahead inflation forecast of 2.7% remained within BSP target tolerance.
96.1% of OFW households allocated remittances to food and household needs.
Borrowing intention index improved to -69.5% for next quarter and -62.1% for next 12 months.
Spending outlook declined to 40.3% for Q2 2026, less upbeat across most consumer items.
Big-ticket buying sentiment improved from -66.2% to -64.0% in current quarter.
limits: Survey captures expectations rather than actual financial behavior or realized spending.
Income group thresholds are static and may not reflect real purchasing power changes over time.
Data does not capture individual-level spending granularity or transaction-level detail.
Sample skewed toward high-income group at 40.3% of respondents.
Survey conducted before Middle East conflict onset, limiting forward-looking applicability.

limitations: Survey captures self-reported expectations rather than actual financial behavior.
High-income group comprises 40.3% of respondents, potentially overrepresenting higher-income perspectives.
Income group thresholds are static and do not adjust for inflation or purchasing power changes.
Data does not capture individual-level spending, transaction details, or budget allocation granularity.
Survey conducted 22 January to 5 February 2026, before the onset of the Middle East conflict. [unacknowledged]
Sample drawn from PSA 2023 Master Sample, which may lag demographic shifts since 2023. [unacknowledged]
